DE-102004033572-A1.one_line_summary: German application (same family content as DE202004010854U1) for a power-assisted distribution/delivery trolley with two hub-motor-driven castors controlled differentially by two handle force gauges, plus safety switching for one-hand release (brake/no drive at standstill, straight-ahead when moving).

E1.quote: and rigid carriers  4  for rear castors  5  and yokes pivotable about vertical axes  6  for front castors  7  includes.
E1.note: Four-wheeled delivery/picking trolley chassis with load area 2: two rear fixed castors 5 and front swivel castors 7 on vertical-axis yokes 6; intended to relieve the operator when moving a heavily loaded cart. Claim 1 requires only at least one swivel castor plus two fixed castors (3 or more wheels).

E2.quote: In both embodiments, with each of the rear fixed castors  5  in each case a direction of rotation reversible, under load starting electric motor  8th
E2.note: Exactly two of the wheels are driven (one reversible electric motor per rear fixed castor), but they have traction drive only, with no steering drive at all, let alone 360 degree steering. Steering comes from differential motor power. The generic claim language says the driven pair may be the fixed or the swivel castors, but even then the swivel is passive, not motor-steered.

E3.quote: and rigid carriers  4  for rear castors  5  and yokes pivotable about vertical axes  6  for front castors  7  includes.
E3.note: The non-driven wheels are free-swivel front castors 7, as in the idea. But the two driven wheels are the rear pair on a common rigid axle 9 (same side, coaxial), not placed diagonally, and they are fixed, so the cart cannot move sideways in any direction.

E4.quote: while the push bar  12  in the embodiment according to  2  illustrated distributor or. Delivery cart with additional, the traverse  14  outstanding handles  15  Is provided.
E4.note: U-shaped push bar 12 (spars 13, crossbar 14) with additional handles 15 that contain the force sensors; sensors built into the push handles.

E5.quote: in the handles  15  Sensors, in particular dynamometers  16  arranged by an operator on one or each of the handles  15  exerted forces, in particular tensile or shear forces, in corresponding control signals
E5.note: Two spaced force gauges 16 in the handles measure push/pull force of each hand and turn it into control signals. But there is no motion vector: each hand's force simply sets its own motor's power (differential push = turning). No explicit use of instantaneous speed or acceleration, and no omnidirectional translation vector.

E6.quote: a control and regulating device for powering the electric motors in relation to each by each of the two hands of the operator on the car exerted shear or traction
E6.note: Per-wheel commands are traction power only, proportional to the force of the corresponding hand (differential drive); steering by differential wheel speed rather than a dedicated per-wheel steering angle. Second switching device equalises both motors for straight-ahead travel when one hand is released.

DE-102004033572-A1.combination_note: Does not disclose E2+E3: the two driven wheels are traction-only fixed castors on one rear axle, not diagonal steer-and-drive modules; only the free-swivel passive castors match. Does not disclose E5->E6 as claimed in the idea: handle forces map directly to two motor powers (differential steering), with no translation vector, no speed/acceleration term and no steering angle. Closest overlap is the force-sensing push handles (E4) and power-assisted heavy trolley with two driven wheels plus swivel castors; the main gap is the diagonal pair of 360 degree steer-and-drive modules and vector-based steering-angle control. Status: withdrawn application, so no claim overlap analysis.

EP-2897566-B1.one_line_summary: Powered patient support apparatus (bed/stretcher/cot) with motor-driven and motor-steered wheels controlled by a force sensing system that measures magnitude, direction and location (moment) of user forces and amplifies the motion the apparatus would naturally make.

E1.quote: patient support apparatus 20a includes four wheels 24, which are each generally positioned adjacent the four corners of apparatus 20a
E1.note: Four-wheeled hospital bed/stretcher/cot base for delicate patient transport.

E2.quote: Patient support apparatus 20e differs from patient support apparatus 20d in that the two driven wheels 24a have been replaced by two steered and driven wheels 24c.
E2.note: FIG. 8 has exactly two steered-and-driven wheels 24c, but on a six-wheel base (four casters 24d plus two 24c), not two of four. FIG. 3/FIG. 6 have four steer-and-drive wheels (24c), not two. 360 degree steering range is not stated.

E3.quote: wheels 24d of apparatus 20e are castered or otherwise free wheeling wheels that rotate to match the current direction of movement
E3.note: Remaining wheels are free-swivel casters, but the two active wheels are not placed diagonally: FIG. 8 derives from FIG. 7 where the active pair sits side-by-side on a common axis. No diagonal arrangement found (grep 'diagonal' returns nothing). Claim 10 and the description only say steerable/powered wheels may be at 'one or more of the corners', a generic teaching, not a diagonal selection; no 'opposite corner' wording either.

E4.quote: Handles 46 include one or more force sensors 52 positioned thereon, or they make pivoting contact with one or more force sensors 52 as a user manipulates them
E4.note: Push handles with built-in force sensors (also side-rail and footboard sensors).

E5.quote: any detected force inputs from force sensors 52 will result in controller 50 causing purely translational motion of the support apparatus if the speed sensor(s) indicates that the support apparatus is currently traveling under a threshold speed
E5.note: Difference: the idea is unconditionally translation-only, while EP is purely translational only below a threshold speed and otherwise adds powered rotation (claim 1 uses the moment of the force to command turning). Otherwise close: handle force (magnitude and direction) is turned into motion with 'a speed or acceleration that generally corresponds to the magnitude of the sensed forces', and the current measured speed is fed to the controller.

E6.quote: controller 50 processes those readings and outputs appropriate steering and/or drive commands to motors 54 and/or 56
E6.note: Per-wheel steering motor 56 and drive motor 54 receive commands derived from the force readings (FIG. 3/4: each wheel has its own steering and power motor).

EP-2897566-B1.combination_note: E2+E3 not disclosed together: the only two-steer-and-drive-wheel embodiment (FIG. 8, apparatus 20e) has four free-wheeling casters (six wheels total) and the active pair is not diagonal; four-wheel embodiments use four steer-and-drive wheels, Ackermann, or a single central wheel. E5->E6 is close: force magnitude/direction -> speed/acceleration -> steering and drive commands per wheel, with a speed-dependent purely translational mode. Closest gap to the idea: the diagonal placement of exactly two swerve modules on a four-wheel base with two free casters, and an unconditional translation-only vector (EP uses moment/rotation in its main claim).

JP-2008137631-A.one_line_summary: Compact transport cart with two electric casters on one diagonal (each a 360-degree swivelling caster with two in-wheel motors, steered by wheel speed difference) and two free casters on the other diagonal.

E1.quote: A pair of electric casters 21 and 22, a pair of free casters 23 and 24, a battery 25 and a control device 26 are disposed on the lower surface of the vehicle body 2.
E1.note: Rectangular four-caster transport cart for parts in factories/warehouses; electric bed and wheelchair are also named as applications.

E2.quote: the support column 31 is supported by a support portion 27 provided on the vehicle body 2 by a bearing (not shown) so as to be able to rotate 360 ° about the vertical axis
E2.note: Exactly two active wheel units that drive and swivel 360 degrees, but the steering comes from the speed difference between a pair of drive wheels inside each caster, not from a dedicated steering motor. The background prior art (JP UM 6-25224) has diagonal drive wheels steered by a steering motor, with 360 degrees not stated.

E3.quote: The free casters 23 and 24 are disposed on the other diagonal line passing through the remaining two corners of the vehicle body 2 and the vehicle body center of gravity C1
E3.note: The electric casters sit on one diagonal and the free casters on the other. The free casters swivel 360 degrees about the vertical axis. Claim 2 also covers this.

E4.quote: As the operation unit, an operation lever that can be tilted in accordance with the traveling direction, a button arranged in accordance with the moving direction, or the like can be used.
E4.note: A tilting lever (joystick-like) on an operation handle on the vehicle body, or wired/wireless. No force sensors in the push handles.

E5.quote: the control apparatus 26 determines a traveling direction by tilting an operation lever. Further, the traveling speed is determined by the inclination angle of the operation lever.
E5.note: The direction and speed command comes from lever tilt, not from measured handle push force, and nothing is said about using the instantaneous speed or acceleration. Rotation in place is also commanded.

E6.quote: when the transport vehicle 1 is moved in an oblique direction or a lateral direction, the two drive wheels 32 and 33 in the electric casters 21 and 23 are rotated at a predetermined rotation speed ratio
E6.note: Each caster is oriented and then driven for oblique or lateral travel, but the orientation is set by the differential wheel speed ratio, not by a commanded steering angle from a steering drive.

JP-2008137631-A.combination_note: E2+E3: largely yes. There are exactly two powered 360-degree swivelling units on one diagonal and two free swivel casters on the other diagonal, and the stated reason is stability when moving obliquely or laterally. The gap is that steering is by differential speed of twin in-wheel motors, with no separate steering motor. The background prior art (diagonal drive wheels steered by a steering motor plus idle wheels) is even closer on E2. E5->E6: not disclosed. The input is lever tilt, with no handle-force sensing and no speed or acceleration term. This is the closest gap to the idea.

JP-2014046890-A.one_line_summary: Power-assist omnidirectional trolley whose load rests on four free casters while spring-loaded, servo-driven omni wheels (four in a rectangle or three in a triangle) move it according to the force on a load-cell handle.

E1.quote: The omnidirectional mobile trolley 1 (hereinafter also referred to as “trolley”) having the power assist function of the present application normally includes four free casters under the pedestal.
E1.note: A cart for heavy loads on four corner casters, but with 3-4 extra omni drive wheels underneath, so it is not a four-wheeled base.

E2.note: Drive is by omni wheels with fixed axles and no steering. The document explicitly avoids steered drive wheels. An omni wheel is not a steer-and-drive wheel.

E3.quote: The carriage 1 of the present application is provided with the free casters 30 at the lower four corners of the carriage 40, the omni wheel 10 is arranged in a rectangular shape below the carriage 40
E3.note: There are free-swivel casters, but four of them (all corners). The active wheels are four omni wheels in a rectangle (diagonal pairs with parallel axles), not two diagonal steer-and-drive wheels.

E4.quote: The handle 20 is connected to the load cell 21 and the handle 20 is operated with three degrees of freedom of the rotation direction θ, the X axis, and the Y axis.
E4.note: A push handle with a grip lever and a 3-axis load cell.

E5.quote: Moreover, the output torque of each drive unit connected to the shaft of the omni wheel has a power assist function that is proportional to the external force applied to the load cell.
E5.note: Handle force (X, Y, rotation) is measured and turned into motion, but the drive torque is simply proportional to force. Instantaneous speed or acceleration is not considered, and rotation is commanded, so the vector is not translation-only.

E6.quote: arithmetic processing is performed by a control unit (not shown), and the rotation speed and rotation are applied to the drive unit connected to the shaft of each omni wheel.
E6.note: Per-wheel commands are only rotation speed and direction of omni wheels. There is no steering angle.

JP-2014046890-A.combination_note: E2+E3: not disclosed. The document uses four (or three) unsteered omni drive wheels plus four free casters and rejects steered drive wheels as slow. E5->E6: partial. Handle force from a load cell drives the wheels with torque proportional to force, but there is no speed/acceleration-aware translation vector and no per-wheel steering angle. The closest gap is the wheel architecture: omni wheels instead of two diagonal swerve wheels.

E1.note: Four-wheeled trolley (2 rear omni wheels + 2 front casters) carrying devices such as an X-ray scanner; heavy-load/hospital-bed context not stated explicitly.

E2.quote: each omnidirectional wheel 3 includes a frame 17, a pair of drive discs 18 rotatably supported by the frame 17, and an annular main wheel 19 disposed between the pair of drive discs 18.
E2.note: Two of four wheels are active, but they are drive-disk omnidirectional wheels, not steer-and-drive wheels with a 360 deg steering drive.

E3.quote: Each caster 13 has a fork 13A rotatably coupled to the arm 14 about an axis extending vertically
E3.note: Passive wheels are swivel casters (front), but the two active wheels are a left/right pair on the rear, not diagonal.

E4.quote: The handle 5 is supported by the handle holder 35 via the force sensor 6
E4.note: Push handle on a three-axis force sensor.

E5.quote: the control device 7 sets the target speed vector provisional value vtp of the vehicle body 2 based on the load detected by the force sensor 6

limitations.quote: A patient support apparatus comprising a frame, a plurality of casters coupled to the frame, a wheel coupled to the frame
limitations.reason: Cart base/frame.

limitations.limitation: a plurality of casters coupled to the frame,
limitations.quote: A patient support apparatus comprising a frame, a plurality of casters coupled to the frame, a wheel coupled to the frame
limitations.reason: Two free-swivel casters.

limitations.limitation: a wheel coupled to the frame,
limitations.quote: A patient support apparatus comprising a frame, a plurality of casters coupled to the frame, a wheel coupled to the frame
limitations.reason: At least one active wheel (the idea has two; 'a wheel' is open-ended).

limitations.limitation: a motor coupled to the wheel and operable to rotate the wheel to propel the patient support apparatus along a floor, the wheel being movable relative to the frame so as to reorient a rotation axis of the wheel relative to the frame thereby to propel the patient support apparatus in different directions that are non-parallel with a longitudinal dimension of the frame,
limitations.quote: a motor coupled to the wheel and operable to rotate the wheel to propel the patient support apparatus along a floor, the wheel being movable relative to the frame so as to reorient a rotation axis of the wheel
limitations.reason: Traction motor plus 360 degree steering reorients the wheel axis to propel in non-longitudinal directions.

limitations.limitation: an electrical system comprising a controller to control operation of the motor, the controller being configured to signal operation of the motor to rotate the wheel to propel the patient support apparatus along the floor,
limitations.quote: an electrical system comprising a controller to control operation of the motor, the controller being configured to signal operation of the motor to rotate the wheel
limitations.reason: The idea has a controller commanding traction drive.

limitations.limitation: a push handle situated near a first end of the frame, and
limitations.quote: a push handle situated near a first end of the frame, and a plurality of user inputs coupled to the push handle
limitations.reason: The idea uses push handles of the cart with built-in sensors.

limitations.limitation: a plurality of user inputs coupled to the push handle, a first user input of the plurality of user inputs being operable by a user to signal the controller to operate the motor to propel the patient support apparatus in a first direction parallel with the longitudinal dimension of the frame, and a second user input of the plurality of user inputs being operable by a user to signal the controller to operate the motor to propel the patient support apparatus in a second direction that is other than the longitudinal dimension relative to the frame, the first user input being spaced apart from the second user input.
limitations.reason: The idea uses one force-sensing handle/joystick that yields a continuous direction vector; it does not specify two spaced-apart inputs, one for longitudinal and one for non-longitudinal propulsion. A two-handle sensor layout could arguably be read on it, so this is uncertain.
